newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine unions sound warning ahead of talks.
newsitem.headline: Argentine unions sound warning ahead of talks.

text.p: Argentina's top trade union chief warned Monday workers will go back on the warparth if talks with government officials and businessmen on labor reforms, planned for February, fall through again.

In an interview with the local daily Clarin, General Labor Confederation (CGT) chief Rodolfo Daer said the ruling Peronist Party would risk a mass vote against them in this year's mid-term elections if the government sticks to its guns on labor reforms.

The CGT staged general strikes in September and December against government bills and decrees that would have curtailed their control over health care plans and their role in collective wage bargaining.
The decrees, signed by President Carlos Menem in December, were overturned by the courts while the bills remain stuck in Congress.
Daer said labor reforms "aim to degrade the life of workers and are the legal tool for a huge cut in salaries."
The government and CGT are scheduled to meet Wednesday to set the agenda for formal negotiations in February.

Daer said if the government sided with industry leaders and antagonized the unions, "dialogue will head straight for failure ... they will push us to protests, and the people will be with us when they vote in October."
The union chief also lambasted businessmen.

"Argentine businessmen are totally fourth-rate. They have no concept of what a country is. During the military dictatorship they became financial speculators, stopped producing to become importers. Then they took advantage of contracts with the state."
Daer called for a broad-based unemployment benefits system and effective measures to reduce unemployment of 17.3 percent.

Asked what would happen if the jobless rate did not come down as a result of labor reforms, Daer said: "It will be a time of popular rebellion, because people get fed up. Unemployment attacks the family ... we agree with Pope John Paul II in that we say NO to ruthless capitalism."
